steps.what: Coordinate work with emergency medical team members, police and fire personnel at the incident

tasks.design: Retain real-time coordination with responders. An existing {OTHER} dispatch system can supply incident information, but its runtime does not replace situational decisions or closed-loop communication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actions depend on changing hazards, patient condition and responder availability.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing communication equipment supports coordination without removing the need to confirm understanding.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting reports, unsafe scenes and rapidly changing priorities.
tasks.human_edge: Shared situational awareness and accountable communication under pressure.
tasks.altitude: No change to coordination time or command authority.

reach.task: Agree patient-care responsibilities during a multi-responder incident
reach.learn: Local command, escalation and clinical scope

evidence.claim: Retaining dynamic responder coordination is an E1 judgement; the digest provides no measured coordination saving.

assumptions: Boundary is the technician's live coordination, excluding dispatch entry and clinical documentation.
Responders produce verbal observations during their existing duties. The technician's confirmation and interpretation stay fully counted; no structured incident flags are assumed.
Zero upkeep because no new software or process is proposed.
research_questions: Where do communication failures occur during multi-responder incidents?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0; live responder coordination is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain vehicles and equipment and replenish supplies

steps.what: Inspect vehicles and medical and communication equipment for readiness
Maintain vehicles and equipment within authorised maintenance limits
Count and replenish first aid equipment and supplies

tasks.design: Retain physical readiness checks, maintenance and replenishment. Instructions may already be held in {DOCS}; putting a checklist on a screen alone earns no saving in the physical work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Condition and stock must be checked at the vehicle, then corrected physically.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported software change removes these physical actions.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting hidden faults and deciding when equipment must be withdrawn.
tasks.human_edge: Hands-on safety checks and recognition of abnormal equipment behaviour.
tasks.altitude: Readiness work and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Confirm critical equipment readiness before deployment
reach.learn: Clinical equipment requirements and fault escalation

evidence.claim: Physical checks, authorised maintenance and replenishment remain manual in this E1 design; no administrative baseline is invented.

assumptions: Boundary is the technician's hands-on readiness work, excluding specialist repairs and purchasing by other roles.

The technician produces condition observations in s1 and stock counts in s3; their capture is fully retained. No existing digital defect codes, live stock balance or structured par levels are assumed.
The technician uses current authorised instructions and manually confirms required quantities. Zero upkeep because no change is introduced.
research_questions: Is there separately measurable duplicate recording outside these physical actions?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=35+40+25=100; gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Inspection, maintenance, counting and replenishment remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe, record and report patient condition and treatment response

steps.what: Observe patient condition, injury and reactions to treatment
Record observations and assemble condition, treatment and reaction details for physician handover
Report patient condition and treatment response to the physician and answer clarifications

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} electronic patient record to reuse technician-entered observations in a handover view. The technician still captures and verifies the clinical facts, approves the exact record, observes changes and gives a live physician handover.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same observations can be copied into multiple record sections and a handover format.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record templates can reuse captured fields without interpreting the patient or changing treatment.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete observations, uncertain timing and deterioration during handover.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising clinical changes and emphasising what the physician needs to hear now.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated transcription; observation and clinical communication remain fully retained.

reach.task: Confirm handover completeness for a transferred patient
reach.learn: Receiving-team information needs and escalation protocol

evidence.claim: Autoscriber summarises consultations into HiX; this demonstrates documentation assistance, not emergency-scene safety or the native-template savings proposed here.
The proposed native reuse of technician-entered fields and its time estimates are E1 assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary includes observation, recording and physician handover, excluding administering treatment and physician labour.

The technician produces patient reference, observation time, condition findings, treatment time and details, and observed reactions through first entry in s2. Capture, identity checks and clinical verification fit within its 15 retained hours; s1 observation remains fully retained.
No free monitor integration, ambient transcript or inferred reaction code is assumed. Missing fields remain manually entered; the template only reuses verified entries.
Test native forms first. Savings require measured duplicate entry within today's s2; if it is already entered once, use the low scenario.
Urgent verbal reporting must not wait for record completion; the ordered graph represents routine completed handover, with immediate escalation taking precedence.
unknowns: Patient record access and native handover views
research_questions: Does template reuse remove duplicate entry after counting initial capture and clinical checking?

already_counted.description: First capture, identity verification and record approval

incremental.description: Maintain template mappings and audit missing handover facts

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient record version, identity, observation times, condition, treatments and reactions; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=50+25*0.60+25=90; gross=10, upkeep=2, net=8. High assumes duplicate transcription; low assumes existing single entry gives zero gross benefit while the 2-hour upkeep remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Hands-on emergency care, coordination and readiness stay human; duplicate record assembly may shrink.
reach: Improve handover completeness with receiving nurses
role.ambitious_version: Use documentation savings to protect attention for observation and handover, subject to validated local workflow.
